main_text.p: frigidioribus, nempe apoplexiam, paraly-sim, epilepsia, catalepsim, & alia id genus. Haec breviter de commodis & incommodis Lunae, e quibus humores nostri corporis, nec alius cuiusvis sanguinei animalis per singula plenilunia non crescere: nec p interlunia ipsos quoq; decrescere, colligere possumus. Adde quod si plenilunio plethora & humorum plenitas esset tribuenda, certe nulla opus foret evacuatione, sed relinquenda esset sequenti, & proximo interlunio: quando videlicet necessario fieret vasorum inanitio. Proinde vana esset nostri boni senis Hippocrat. doctrina, qua passim, & præsertim[?] suis in aphorismis plethora evacuatione per sanguinis emissionem, ut & cacochymiam purgatione esse soluendam docemur. Nec præterea audiendi sunt, qui acutorum morborum crises ipsius Lunae ui & motui attribuunt.

Nam si id esset, profecto exquisitae (exempli causa) omnes tertianae, quæ eodem tempore quoslibet invadunt, eodem æque momento indicarentur. Sed alias alijs celerius (licet eadem hora simul inceperint, uariosque invaserint) & alias tardius iudicari, finiriq; norut[?] satis omnes medici. Propte-
Cf. the printed text above for the catchword "rea", which begins the following page.

page.notes: Page number "65" is printed at the top right; the final digit is partly unclear, hence [?]. "vasorum" is read from a damaged word and is uncertain; the printed letters look like "uasorum". "præsertim" and "norut" are doubtful readings. The line ending "Propte-" continues on the next page, with "rea" as the catchword. The printed "ple-thora" and "paraly-sim" are line-end hyphenations kept as printed.
